headline: President Bush set up a federal emergency board to look into a labor dispute between SEPTA and its train engineers' union.
what_it_does: This order created an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) and its locomotive engineers, who are represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen. Emergency boards like this are typically used under federal railway labor law to study a dispute and make recommendations. While a board does its work, a strike or lockout is generally put on hold for a set period.

who_it_affects.how: Their labor dispute with SEPTA was sent to a federal board for investigation, which typically delays any strike while the board works.
The transit agency's dispute with its engineers' union came under review by a presidential emergency board.

who_it_affects.group: Commuter rail riders in the Philadelphia area
who_it_affects.how: Setting up the board likely delayed a possible work stoppage that could have disrupted their train service.
